title: Japan Student Visa Part-Time Work Rules: What Actually Changed in 2026
summary: The 28-hour cap did not change in 2026. How schools verify it did — they now ask every student for daily hours and every workplace, four times a year.
body_html:
Most English guides still describe the situation before the revision. The headline number is unchanged, so the pages look current. They are not.

What changed is not the limit. It is the verification.

The cap itself is unchanged

Under the general work permit, a student may work up to 28 hours per week. [source:2] During the school's long vacation periods that becomes up to 8 hours per day. [source:2]

Nothing in the 2026 revision touches those figures. [source:1] If you read an older guide and remembered 28, you remembered correctly.

Your school now asks you four questions, four times a year [source:1]

From 2026, schools that enrol international students are asked to confirm the following from each enrolled student once every 3 months. [source:1] The method is left to the school, but the four items are specified:

  1. Whether you hold a work permit at all. [source:1]
  2. The name of every place you work — all of them, if there is more than one. [source:1]
  3. What the work actually consists of. [source:1]
  4. Your daily working hours. [source:1]

Read the fourth one again. Not your weekly total — your hours per day. [source:1]

This is the practical change, and it is the one no summary mentions. A weekly figure can be reconstructed from memory. A day-by-day record cannot. If you are working two jobs and have never written down which days you worked where, the first of these checks will be uncomfortable.

Start keeping the record now, before the question arrives. A note on your phone is enough. You are not required to produce a formal document — the guidance leaves the method open — but you are expected to be able to answer.

What happens if the check finds a problem

Where a school finds a situation that breaches the terms of the permit, it is asked to advise the student, have the situation corrected immediately, and then confirm that it has been. [source:1] The results of these checks and any guidance given are to be kept on record. [source:1]

So the first check is not automatically a report to immigration. The sequence is: find it, fix it, verify the fix. A problem caught and corrected stays inside the school.

The clause about your employer

One line in the guidance is worth knowing about, because it is not in any English summary I could find.

The agency gives an explicit example of when a school should pass information to the immigration office: when a student reports that the employer is forcing them to work more than 28 hours a week. [source:1] The other named case is a student who does not improve after being advised. [source:1]

Two things follow from that.

First, "my employer made me" is a situation the guidance names directly. It is not an excuse you would be inventing — the agency anticipated it.

Second, be clear-eyed about where the information goes. It goes to the immigration office, which is also the authority over your own status. This is not a complaints channel that protects you and penalises the employer; it is a reporting channel about a situation you are part of.

The practical conclusion is the same either way: if an employer is pushing you past the limit, raise it with your school early and on your own initiative, rather than letting it surface at a quarterly check.

Two things that are less absolute than you have read

English guides tend to present the cap as having no exceptions. The source text is more specific.

Delivery and gig work. Working as an individual contractor — taking delivery jobs and being paid per result — is covered by the general permit, provided the working hours can be objectively confirmed. [source:2] It is not a separate category that falls outside the system, and it is not automatically prohibited either.

Practicum that counts for credit. Where a practicum is required to earn credit and is closely related to your field of study, permission can be granted for more than 28 hours per week. [source:2] That is a separate, individual permission — not something your existing permit covers — so it has to be applied for. But it exists, and "28 hours, no exceptions" is not what the rule says. [source:2]

The other 2026 change: proving Japanese ability [source:1]

This one is about getting in, not about working, but it is part of the same revision and affects anyone applying now.

Previously, a record of 150 hours of Japanese study was accepted as evidence of A1-level ability at the application stage. [source:1] That route is closed. A test certificate or a confirmation by interview is now required. [source:1]

The timing is in two parts. [source:1] For Certificate of Eligibility applications, it applies to students planning to enrol from October 2026 onwards. [source:1] For change-of-status and extension applications, it applies to applications filed from 1 July 2026. [source:1]

Both of those dates have passed. If you are applying now, this already applies to you.

There is one exemption: applicants from the countries and regions on the agency's published list who graduated from a foreign higher education institution and submit the graduation certificate are not required to prove Japanese ability. [source:1] Whether your nationality is on that list is a question for the school handling your application.

What to do

  • Keep a daily record of hours and workplace, starting now. The check asks for daily hours. [source:1]
  • If you work more than one job, list them all. The guidance asks for every workplace. [source:1]
  • If an employer is pushing you over the limit, tell your school first — before a check finds it.
  • If you are applying for a visa now, ask your school which route they are using to evidence your Japanese: test certificate, or interview. [source:1] One of the two has to be recorded.

Rules are applied case by case and the official texts are the only authority. Both sources are linked below — read them, or have your school walk you through the parts that affect you. This page summarises; it does not advise.

claims_without_sources: 「英文内容普遍还是旧版信息」—— SERP で実際に確認した印象だが、網羅的調査ではないため本文では「most English guides」と程度を限定し、数で裏づけるような書き方はしていない。
罰則・在留資格取消の具体的要件 —— 本通知には書かれていない。別の法令の話なので、推測で書かず一切触れていない。
３か月ごとの確認で学生が提出すべき書類の形式 —— 通知は「任意の方法により」としか書いておらず様式を定めていない。したがって「スマホのメモで足りる」は通知が方法を定めていないことの帰結として書き、書式要件があるかのようには書いていない。
雇用主からの強要が報告された後に当局が何をするか —— 通知は報告までしか書いていない。その先を推測せず、「情報がどこへ行くか」という事実だけを述べた。
別表掲載国・地域の具体的な国名 —— 当庁 HP の別表を確認していないため列挙していない。「学校に確認せよ」とした。
